summary_html: A **judge orders** CPS to investigate or assess during civil/criminal proceedings. Federal funding statutes (ASFA/IV-E) tether court findings to child-welfare actions, embedding judicial oversight into intake-to-case flow. In Alabama the age of majority is 19 (Ala. Code § 26-1-1), and for child abuse and neglect reporting a "child" is a person under 18, or a person under 19 who is in need of protective services and does not qualify for adult protective services (Ala. Code § 26-14-1(3)). Alabama is not a universal-reporter state: Ala. Code § 26-14-3 sets out who must report, and Ala. Code § 26-14-4 permits any other person to report if they have reasonable cause to suspect a child is being abused or neglected, without requiring it.

The hearing package (counsel, witnesses, cross-examination, subpoenas, exculpatory evidence, an impartial hearing officer, and 10 departmental working days to request the hearing in writing) runs only to a person who "is employed by, serves as a volunteer for, holds a license or certificate for, or is connected with any facility, agency, or home which cares for and controls any children" that is licensed, approved, certified, state-operated, or exempt from licensing; a parent investigated in their own home is not in that class

Ala. Code § 26-14-1(3) — "CHILD" for child abuse and neglect reporting: a person under 18, or a person under 19 who is in need of protective services and does not qualify for adult protective services under Title 38, Chapter 9
Ala. Code § 26-1-1 — Age of majority designated as 19 years
Ala. Code § 26-14-4 — Permissive reporting: any person may report if he or she has reasonable cause to suspect that a child is being abused or neglected
